candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, Appendix A, printed p.20 / PDF p.24, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: 'Utilize the rights of delegation (e.g., right task, right circumstances, right person, right direction/communication, right supervision/evaluation)'
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Assignment, Delegation and Supervision
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate the 'right task' from the other rights of delegation by confirming that the activity is permitted by the delegatee's role and the practice setting's established policies and procedures.

options.A: The activity is within the delegatee's job description or the setting's established written policies and procedures
options.B: The client's condition is stable and the delegation remains appropriate if the condition does not change
options.C: The delegatee has the knowledge and skills required to perform the activity safely
options.D: The RN gives patient-specific instructions and explains what information must be reported back

candidate.rationale: NCSBN's Five Rights of Delegation table defines right task by whether the activity falls within the delegatee's job description or established written policies and procedures of the practice setting. B describes right circumstance, C describes right person, and D describes right directions and communication. Therefore A is the single best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Right task concerns whether the activity falls within the delegatee's job description or established written policies/procedures; client stability is right circumstance, competence is right person, and patient-specific instructions/reporting are right directions and communication.
candidate.source_locator: Table 1, 'Five Rights of Delegation,' Journal of Nursing Regulation p.8: Right task; Right circumstance; Right person; Right directions and communication
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.source_version_date: April 2016 guideline currently linked from the NCSBN Delegation page; accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: An RN is deciding whether a nursing activity meets the 'right task' element of the Five Rights of Delegation. Which finding best addresses the right task?
